channel.title: Research Notes — The Stereograph Archive
channel.description: Real places, real photographs, and the people who worked them, with sources listed and every card linked back to the archive.

item.title: Mauch Chunk, the town that sold the slope three times
item.description: A town in a gorge learned to sell the slope it was stuck on: first as a coal road, then as a ride, then as a name.

item.title: Isles of Shoals, where a garden outlived the hotels
item.description: The Shoals were kept alive twice by selling a stay on rocks that could not feed themselves: first by a hotel and a garden, then by conferences and a marine laboratory.

item.title: Delaware Water Gap, where the river kept the valley
item.description: Hotel keepers turned a river notch into a season, and a government tried to turn the valley into a lake. The hotels burned, the lake was never built, and the river is still there.

item.title: Crawford Notch, where the house outlived the family
item.description: A narrow gap in the White Mountains was opened three times, by a horse trail, by inns and a footpath, and by a railroad shelf blasted into a cliff, and each opening cost its builders something different.

item.title: Watkins Glen, where every waterfall got a name before it got a staircase
item.description: A newspaper editor named every fall in the gorge and sold tickets to see them. A painter came to paint one fall and stayed twenty years, and his son photographed the same falls. The names, the pictures, and the stone walk are what survive.
